Physics Curriculum Schedule (May to June 6th)

Week 1 (May 6-10)

Monday: Introduction to Geometric Optics - Reflection laws and ray diagrams Wednesday: Refraction and Snell’s Law, Total Internal Reflection Friday: Thin Lens Equation, problem-solving with lenses and mirrors

Homework: Problem Set 1 - Geometric Optics applications

### Week 2 (May 13-17)

Monday: Review Problem Set 1, Introduction to Wave Optics - Interference Wednesday: Double-slit experiment, diffraction patterns Friday: Polarization and Malus’ Law, Lab demonstration if possible

Homework: Problem Set 2 - Wave Optics problems

Week 3 (May 20-24)

Monday: Review Problem Set 2, Introduction to Electrostatics Wednesday: Electric charge, Coulomb’s Law, Electric fields Friday: Electric potential, capacitance basics

Homework: Problem Set 3 - Electrostatics problems

Week 4 (May 27-31)

Monday: Review Problem Set 3, Introduction to DC Circuits Wednesday: Current, resistance, Ohm’s Law Friday: Series/parallel circuits, Kirchhoff’s Rules

Homework: Problem Set 4 - Circuit analysis problems

Week 5 (June 3-7)

Monday: Review Problem Set 4, Magnetic fields and forces Wednesday: Electromagnetic induction, Faraday’s Law Thursday/Friday (June 6): EM waves and connections to optics, Course review Final Assessment: Comprehensive test (if needed) or Final Project due

Teaching Strategies to Maximize Time:

Flipped Classroom Components: Assign reading or video tutorials before introducing new topics Focused Problem Sets: Limit to 5-7 high-quality problems that target essential skills In-Class Practice: Use 15-20 minutes of class time for guided practice Concept Connections: Regularly highlight connections between topics Visual Demonstrations: Use simulations or quick demos to reinforce concepts Formative Assessment: Use entrance/exit tickets to quickly check understanding

Time-Saving Tips:

Create a one-page formula sheet for students to use Focus lab activities on conceptual understanding rather than extensive data collection Use online simulations (like PhET) to demonstrate concepts quickly Prepare condensed handouts with key definitions and examples Consider a final project that integrates multiple concepts rather than separate assessments for each unit

Lecture Files to Create Geometric Optics (### Week 1)

Lecture 1A: Reflection Fundamentals

Law of reflection Ray diagrams for plane and curved mirrors Real vs. virtual images Visual demonstrations/simulations

Lecture 1B: Refraction and TIR

Snell’s Law derivation and applications Index of refraction in different materials Critical angle and total internal reflection Practical applications (fiber optics, prisms)

Lecture 1C: Lenses and Optical Systems

Thin lens equation Ray tracing for converging/diverging lenses Magnification calculations Real-world optical systems (cameras, eyes, telescopes)

Wave Optics (### Week 2)

Lecture 2A: Wave Interference

Young’s double-slit experiment Constructive/destructive interference Path difference and phase relationships Interference patterns and fringe spacing

Lecture 2B: Diffraction and Polarization

Single-slit diffraction Diffraction gratings and spectra Polarization basics Malus’ Law and applications

Electrostatics (### Week 3)

Lecture 3A: Electric Charge and Coulomb’s Law

Electric charge properties Coulomb’s Law and calculations Superposition principle Conservation of charge

Lecture 3B: Electric Fields and Potential

Electric field concept and calculations Field lines representation Electric potential energy and voltage Capacitors and energy storage

DC Circuits (### Week 4)

Lecture 4A: Current and Resistance

Electric current Ohm’s Law Resistivity and resistance Power in circuits

Lecture 4B: Circuit Analysis

Series and parallel connections Kirchhoff’s laws Circuit problem-solving strategies Practical circuit applications

Electromagnetism (### Week 5)

Lecture 5A: Magnetic Fields and Forces

Magnetic field sources Forces on moving charges Forces on current-carrying wires Right-hand rules

Lecture 5B: Electromagnetic Induction and EM Waves

Faraday’s Law Lenz’s Law Electromagnetic waves Connecting optics and electromagnetism

Problem Sets to Create Problem Set 1: Geometric Optics

Problem 1.1: Ray tracing for plane mirrors (image location) Problem 1.2: Ray tracing for curved mirrors (concave/convex) Problem 1.3: Snell’s Law calculations with multiple boundaries Problem 1.4: Critical angle and TIR applications Problem 1.5: Thin lens equation applications Problem 1.6: Integrated problem involving both mirrors and lenses Application Problem: Design a simple optical system (telescope or microscope)

Problem Set 2: Wave Optics

Problem 2.1: Double-slit interference pattern calculations Problem 2.2: Interference with path length differences Problem 2.3: Single-slit diffraction pattern Problem 2.4: Diffraction grating wavelength determination Problem 2.5: Malus’ Law and polarization intensity Application Problem: CD/DVD diffraction analysis

Problem Set 3: Electrostatics

Problem 3.1: Coulomb’s Law with multiple charges Problem 3.2: Electric field calculations for point and distributed charges Problem 3.3: Electric potential and potential difference Problem 3.4: Electric potential energy calculations Problem 3.5: Capacitance calculations (parallel plate) Application Problem: Photocopier or electrostatic precipitator analysis

Problem Set 4: DC Circuits

Problem 4.1: Current and resistance calculations Problem 4.2: Series and parallel resistance networks Problem 4.3: Kirchhoff’s Laws in multi-loop circuits Problem 4.4: Power and energy transfer in circuits Problem 4.5: RC circuits (if time permits) Application Problem: Design a voltage divider or simple alarm circuit

Problem Set 5: Electromagnetism (Optional/Shorter)

Problem 5.1: Magnetic force on moving charges Problem 5.2: Magnetic field calculations Problem 5.3: Electromagnetic induction problems Problem 5.4: EM spectrum and wave properties Application Problem: Generator or transformer analysis

Supplementary Materials

Formula Sheet - One-page reference with all essential equations Concept Map - Visual connections between optics and electromagnetism Review Guide - Summary of key concepts for final assessment Simulation Links - Curated list of PhET or other online simulations Real-world Applications Document - Connecting theory to technology

Lab Activities (If Time Permits)

Mini-Lab: Snell’s Law - Use laser pointers and acrylic blocks Mini-Lab: Diffraction - Measure wavelength using laser and diffraction grating Mini-Lab: Simple Circuits - Build and measure series/parallel circuits Demonstration: Electromagnetic Induction - Solenoid and magnet demonstration
